title: Semantic release v1
description:
How analytics-dbt publishes a semantic release and how metrics-gateway finds the one to serve. Layout in the releases bucket (`semantic_releases_bucket`), per project (`olist`, `funnel`):

  <project>/<sha>/bundle.tar.gz   dbt_project.yml, profiles.yml, models/ and semantic YAML as built, target/semantic_manifest.json, target/manifest.json, and target/osi_document.json when dbt emits one
  <project>/<sha>/release.json    #/$defs/release — written LAST by analytics-dbt; its presence means the bundle is complete
  <project>/current.json          #/$defs/current — written ONLY by metrics-gateway's indexer, after the index for <sha> is ready

analytics-dbt publishes only after `dbt build` succeeded for that project, so no release names a table that does not exist. It never writes current.json. The indexer indexes a published release, then moves current.json to it; the gateway serves exactly current.json's sha. profiles.yml reads every credential from env vars and has two targets, `build` (writer) and `serve` (read-only role with an engine time limit). The sha is supplied to the build as RELEASE_SHA — on a deployed environment, the analytics-dbt commit the image was built from; a release is immutable — once <sha>/release.json exists, a publish of that sha leaves the release untouched and succeeds (every deploy re-runs the job; dbt still builds the tables). Re-indexing the sha already in current.json is likewise a no-op.

files.description: sha256 of each file in the bundle that the gateway reads, keyed by its path inside the bundle. The gateway refuses a bundle whose files do not match.
